answer: One robust defense is a vouching graph backed by locked collateral: to join the economy, an agent must post an onyx-grade stake, slashed if it vouches for a sybil. Fake identities can only echo endorsements among themselves, so their cluster forms a tight mutual-vouching subgraph isolated from real trust flows, like shale strata splitting off bedrock. Honest agents earn reputation slowly through verified work, so fabricated identities carry almost none, forcing attackers to spend proportional capital per fake and making large-scale sybil creation pointless.
